answer.rationale: With the primary contract lapsing in 14 days, no auto-renew, and the line already running at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, any disruption to primary supply carries outsized cost relative to the 18% spend-cut target. memory_c2 (switch_primary_vendor) is the most tempting lever for hitting the finance mandate, but its 'quick onboarding' claim needs verification before betting the only decision slot on it under a hard 14-day deadline with no slack for a hiccup — hence flagging it for the single verification pull. Absent confirmation that a new vendor can be qualified and flowing parts within the window without risking the 94%-utilized line, the safer play this cycle is renew_incumbent, consistent with memory_c1's record of stable integration and uninterrupted deliveries across renewal cycles. This does not solve the cost mandate — the incumbent has already refused to reopen price — so that gap is explicitly carried forward rather than resolved. Switching vendors, adding a second source, or restructuring terms all remain live options for the next review once verified and once there is slack to absorb transition risk.
